objections.raw_quote: The only thing is just the timing, because I got a trip to Europe coming up, and then I've got a jujitsu camp coming up, and those are both pretty expensive. Um, so, this would be eating into both of those budgets for sure, and I'm pretty budget savvy. So that's the only thing that's coming up for me right now.
objections.rep_response: Ran no timing play. Made small talk about the Europe trip, then cut scope and price: 'Tell you what? There's a three-month option that you could do, because for the three months, it's going to be 4K.'

offer.payment_plan_terms: For the six-month $6,000 programme the rep offered: upfront on credit card (stated as what most clients do); an interest-free split in half; or Pava third-party financing over three months at $2,300/month ($6,900), six months at $1,200/month ($7,200) or twelve months at $650/month ($7,800). None of those totals was stated. The prospect asked directly what the interest rate was and the rep answered with monthly figures instead of a rate. In the end the prospect took the three-month $4,000 tier and paid upfront by credit card on the call.

prospect_financials.note: No financial picture was taken. The only disclosure was volunteered: 'I have, I definitely have the money' and 'financially, I'm in a much better place now.' Competing committed spend was a Europe trip and a jiu-jitsu camp, both described as expensive.

evidence: Payment taken on the call by credit card and confirmed: 'Hey, give me one sec, I need to grab my credit card.' then 'Oh, okay. I see it went through.'

Onboarding call with Trevor booked for Tuesday June 30th at 2.45pm Mountain Time and the Zoom confirmation read back by the prospect: 'Hey, Tyler, meeting's been scheduled Tuesday, June 30th at 2.45 p.m. Got the Zoom link.'
Agreement email located: 'You were invited to review and sign a document, this one?' — 'Yep.'
Skool community link and pre-call onboarding form both pointed to in the welcome email.

outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor Tuesday June 30th, 2.45pm Mountain Time. Prospect to complete the onboarding form beforehand, sign the agreement and join the Skool community.

notable.note: Price moved from $6,000 to $4,000 in roughly four minutes, triggered by a discretionary-spend conflict (a Europe trip and a jiu-jitsu camp) rather than by any inability to pay — the prospect had already said 'I definitely have the money.' No timing play was run; the rep cut scope instead. The guarantee that the same rep described the same week as the defining difference between the six- and three-month tiers was never mentioned here, so the prospect chose the un-guaranteed tier without knowing a guarantee existed. Most seriously, at 00:42:09, after payment had already gone through, the prospect disclosed 'CrossFit up my lower back pretty bad... I can't squat, I can't do barbell squats anymore, actually, because of it.' The rep's entire response was 'Oh, damn,' and the conversation moved to hiking.

quality.notes: Extensive inversion. Clear examples: at 00:23:14-00:23:19 'Because how old are you?' is labelled to the prospect and '29' to the rep, when the rep is plainly asking and the prospect answering — the rep's next line is 'When I was 29, I could party... but over 30, and then when I hit 40'. At 00:37:20-00:37:35 'I'm in Poland' is labelled to the rep (correct) but 'So my brother is moving to Turkey. He's in the Air Force' is also labelled to the rep when it is the prospect. The 00:36:23-00:36:39 block, containing 'you need an answer today?', 'I don't want to chase you down' and 'We have a busy schedule', is scrambled badly enough that speaker attribution within it is uncertain, though the phrasing matches the rep's identical line on the Maz call. Roles read from content throughout. The rep confirms his own identity here more clearly than anywhere else in the batch: he is 43, in Krakow, southern Poland, started with Primal Instinct last year through a mutual friend of a sales manager.
